text: Two threads run the same recursive method simultaneously. What do they share and what do they not?
choices: They share the frames of any method marked `static`, since static methods have no receiver.
They share the heap, so any objects reached are common; each has its own stack, so their locals and their recursion depths are independent.
They share the stack, so their recursion depths add and overflow arrives sooner.
They share nothing, since each thread is given a complete copy of the program's memory.
explanation: This is the division that generates every problem in Chapter 31. Locals are private because each thread has its own stack — which is why a pure function is automatically thread-safe and why Chapter 26's parallel counter only broke when it reached through an array reference into the heap. Nothing about `static` changes where locals live; it changes only whether there is a receiver.
